issues.title: Scaffold repository tooling
issues.body:
## User story

As a contributor, I want the repository rules, hooks and CI in place so that every change runs through an issue, a branch, the full test gate and a pull request.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.claude/settings.json`, `hooks/{branch-guard,gate-layers,issue-context}.sh` and the branch-guard test suite are in place and pass
- [ ] `.claude/skills/gh/SKILL.md` describes the issue, branch and PR workflow for `Cloudster1/Exciter` with milestones `M0 Foundation` to `M4 Stator integration` and `Backlog`
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` covers containers only (Makefile, Go 1.26), issue branches, four test layers, `make openapi`, no mocks below the layer under test, style rules, and where Armature and Stator live for reference
- [ ] No other requirements-management product is named anywhere: code, docs, issues, PRs, commits
- [ ] `run-tests.sh` is the single gate: shell tests, Go format/vet/unit, OpenAPI drift, web lint/types/vitest, compose-backed integration and Playwright; `EXCITER_GATE=full` runs everything
- [ ] `Makefile` includes `mk/*.mk`, and each layer joins the gate with the change that introduces its target: `mk/go.mk` with #3, `mk/web.mk`, `mk/biome.mk` and `biome.json` with #6
- [ ] `release.sh` and its tests are ported; `VERSION` is 0.1.0; `CHANGELOG.md` follows Keep a Changelog
- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `./run-tests.sh` in a layer matrix; `release.yml`, issue templates (feature, bug) and a PR template with `Closes #` exist
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/decisions.md` record the architecture and the first decisions: requirement key shape `CHK-R42`, revision equals normative save, the port base, org-wide status category of linked issues, the licence
- [ ] `NOTICE` credits the Apache-2.0 code adapted from Armature and from Stator, naming the source commit

## Tests

`.claude/hooks/tests/branch-guard-test.sh`, `tests/test-ci.sh` (CI jobs cover every layer) and `tests/test-release.sh` run inside `run-tests.sh` and in CI.

## Implementation

- Port from Stator: `.claude/`, `run-tests.sh`, `Makefile`, `release.sh`, `.github/`, `tests/test-ci.sh`, `tests/test-release.sh`, `scripts/test-summary.sh`. Rename `stator`/`STATOR_` to `exciter`/`EXCITER_`.
- `CLAUDE.md` adapted from Stator's; reference paths point at `~/repos/Armature` and a Stator checkout.
- `docs/decisions.md` starts with the decisions listed above; `docs/architecture.md` uses Stator's section skeleton (Overview, Backend, Frontend, Armature integration, Testing, Deployment).
- Licensing gate: Stator is being relicensed to Apache-2.0. Until that relicense is on Stator `main`, port only code whose original is in Armature (Apache-2.0). Stator-only files wait for it, and `NOTICE` names the post-relicense Stator commit each ported file came from.

Paths: `S/` is Stator, `A/` is Armature.

issues.title: Compose stack and Makefile with containerised toolchains
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want one command to start the whole stack on ports that never collide with a Stator checkout so that Exciter, Stator and Armature run side by side.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `make up` / `make down` / `make clean` run the compose stack: Postgres primary and replica, Valkey, SeaweedFS, Mailpit, Keycloak. migrate, seed and api join with #3, the worker with #4, web with #6
- [ ] Ports derive from a hash of the checkout path: base 10000, 500 slots of 20; nothing reaches Stator's 20000-29999 or the kernel's ephemeral range (32768+)
- [ ] Slots containing 16686, 11211, 15672 or 10250 are skipped
- [ ] Each worktree gets its own compose project `exciter-<hash>`
- [ ] `deploy/keycloak/realm.json` defines realm `suite-dev` with clients `exciter`, `armature` and `stator` and the dev users, so one person is the same subject in all three products
- [ ] Postgres roles `exciter_app` (RLS bound) and `exciter_admin` are created by the init script
- [ ] `.cache/stack.env` publishes the `EXCITER_*` URLs and ports for the test layers

## Tests

Shell: `tests/test-ports.sh` checks every computed slot is below 32768, outside 20000-29999 and off the denylist.

## Implementation

- Port `S/mk/stack.mk` (re-based), `S/deploy/docker-compose.yml`, `S/deploy/postgres/{init-roles.sh,replica-entrypoint.sh}`, `S/deploy/Dockerfile.{backend,web}`.
- Realm users mirror Stator's `deploy/keycloak/realm.json`.
- Licensing gate: Stator is being relicensed to Apache-2.0. Until that relicense is on Stator `main`, port only code whose original is in Armature (Apache-2.0). Stator-only files wait for it, and `NOTICE` names the post-relicense Stator commit each ported file came from.

Paths: `S/` is Stator, `A/` is Armature.

issues.title: Backend skeleton: config, database, migrations, HTTP route table
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want a Go service skeleton that mirrors Armature and Stator so that every later feature plugs into the same patterns.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mk/go.mk` and `scripts/go-test.sh` ported from Stator; `check-go` and `test-integration` join the gate
- [ ] `backend/cmd/{api,migrate,openapi,seed}` build
- [ ] `deploy/Dockerfile.backend`; compose gains `migrate`, `seed` and `api` (from Stator's compose), and `mk/stack.mk` gains `DOCKER_GO_STACK` for the integration suite
- [ ] Configuration from `EXCITER_*` environment variables only, with validation and sentence-style errors
- [ ] `internal/db` cluster with primary/replica transactions, read-your-writes via LSN, and org row-level security via `current_org_id()`; IDs from `uuidv7()`
- [ ] Tables use `PRIMARY KEY (org_id, id)` with composite foreign keys and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY
- [ ] goose migrations embedded and applied by `cmd/migrate`; migration 00001 creates `org`, `app_user`, `org_member`, `current_org_id()`, `current_actor_id()` and `set_updated_at()`
- [ ] chi router with the middleware chain (request id, metrics, logging, recovery, security headers, same-site check, timeout, authenticate) and a single error envelope `{code, message, fields?, requestId?}`
- [ ] The route table generates `api/openapi.json` and `web/src/api/schema.d.ts`; operations may be `pending: true` and answer 501
- [ ] A unit test fails when the committed spec is stale and when router and table disagree
- [ ] `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/metrics` and `GET /api/v1/meta` respond

## Tests

Unit: config, LSN, route table drift. Integration: RLS isolates two orgs even through raw SQL as `exciter_app`; the contract test validates every response against `api/openapi.json`; the coverage test refuses a run that left an operation unexercised.

## Implementation

- Port `S/backend/internal/{config,db,freshness,tenant,secret,keyset,openapi,observability,testorg}`.
- Port `S/backend/internal/httpapi/{router,openapi,middleware,errors,request,freshness,observe,edges,test_handlers}.go`, which bring the `operation` struct with `pending`, `tool` and `toolHelp`.
- Port `S/backend/test/{contract_test,zz_coverage_test}.go` and `S/backend/migrations/00001_foundation.sql` (trimmed).
- Originals: `A/backend/internal/db`, `A/backend/internal/freshness`, `A/backend/internal/httpapi/openapi_operations.go`.

Paths: `S/` is Stator, `A/` is Armature.

issues.title: Transactional outbox, worker and audit log
issues.body:
## User story

As a developer, I want events written in the same transaction as the change and an audit log admins can read so that integrations and notifications never act on a rolled-back change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `events.Emit(ctx, tx, topic, payload)` writes to `outbox_event` in the caller's transaction
- [ ] Compose gains the `worker` service
- [ ] `cmd/worker` claims events with `SKIP LOCKED`, retries with backoff and sets an event aside after `MaxAttempts`, recording it in the audit log
- [ ] `exciter_app` may insert an event only with its own actor id
- [ ] `audit_log` is written with the act, readable only by owners and admins, never updated or deleted, pruned after `EXCITER_RETAIN_AUDIT`; `GET /audit`, `/audit/facets` and `/audit/export` are agreed in the route table as pending (served with #5, screen with #6)

## Tests

Unit: backoff. Integration: an event rolls back with its transaction; two workers never claim the same event; the audit row is enforced through SQL.

## Implementation

- Port `S/backend/internal/{events,audit}`, `S/backend/cmd/worker`, `S/web/src/routes/audit.tsx`.
- Migrations 00020 `outbox_event` (from `S/00150_outbox.sql`) and 00021 `audit_log` (from `S/00230_audit_log.sql`).
- Originals: `A/backend/internal/events`, `A/backend/internal/audit`.

Paths: `S/` is Stator, `A/` is Armature.

## Depends on

- #3

issues.title: Requirements: create, edit, trash and revisions
issues.body:
## User story

As an author, I want to write a requirement with a statement and rationale and have every change kept as a revision so that nothing said is ever lost and later reviews, baselines and links can point at an exact revision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Requirement key `<PROJECT>-R<n>` (for example `CHK-R42`), regex `^([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9})-R([1-9][0-9]*)$`, allocated per project
- [ ] Title, rich-text statement, rationale, owner, priority; created and edited with the shared editor
- [ ] A save whose normative content (title, statement, rationale, type, attributes) changed writes an immutable `requirement_revision`; other changes (status, owner, labels, position) go to `requirement_change`
- [ ] Optimistic concurrency: a stale save is refused with 409 and names what to do
- [ ] Trash and restore; purge by admins
- [ ] `/r/{id}` permalink redirects to the current key URL
- [ ] Old keys keep resolving after a move or project key rename

## Tests

Unit: key parsing, normative hash is stable under key order and whitespace, and no Armature or Stator issue-key pattern matches an Exciter key. Integration: revisions cannot be updated or deleted as `exciter_app`; numbers have no gaps; 409 on conflict. Vitest: editor allowlist. Playwright: `requirement-crud.spec.ts`.

## Implementation

- New `backend/internal/requirement` (`requirement.go`, `service.go`, `revision.go`, `trash.go`).
- Revision sequence trigger from `S/backend/migrations/00070_versions.sql`; old keys from `A/backend/migrations/00922_issue_old_keys.sql`; trash from `S/00022_trash.sql`; plain text from `page_plain_blocks` in `S/00100_search.sql`.
- Editor: slimmed port of `S/web/src/features/editor/{Editor,Toolbar,DocView,MentionList}.tsx` and `S/backend/internal/document/{validate,allowlist,text}.go`.
- Migrations 00120-00139. UI `/p/$projectKey/r/$reqKey`.

Paths: `S/` is Stator, `A/` is Armature.

## User story

As a project admin, I want requirements to move through a configurable workflow so that everyone knows whether a requirement is a draft, approved, implemented or verified.

## User story

issues.title: Remove organizations: one installation is one team's requirements
issues.body:
## Why

Exciter is self-hosted, and an installation serves one team, as Armature has decided in its Cloudster1/Armature#208 and Stator in praetorianer777/Stator#380. Organizations add a layer such an installation never uses: an organization to type at sign-in and for single sign-on, switching between organizations, rules for people in several of them, and a tenant column on every table. This epic removes organizations from everything people and the API see, then from the schema.

It runs before the rest of M2, so #28 to #31 are built without organizations rather than reworked.

## Decisions

1. **Product first, schema last.** The product and the API lose organizations while one `org` row stays inside, so `org_id` and row security keep working. The last ticket drops the tenant layer. Every ticket keeps every layer of `./run-tests.sh` green.
2. **A database with several organizations is refused, not merged.** A migration counts them and stops, naming the first ten and saying to delete the extra ones first. Project keys, statuses, workflows and people would collide in a merge.
3. **Everyone signed in belongs to the installation.** Someone without an active membership is refused with "Your account has been switched off. Ask an administrator."
4. **Tests isolate by unique people, project keys and names**, with a serial lane for the tests that change installation-wide settings: single sign-on, the default theme, link types for all projects, all tokens and the Armature connection.
5. **Row security stays for the permission walls.** Exciter's guards live in restrictive policies; only the tenant isolation and administrator bypass policies go with `org_id`.

**What stays, under plainer names:** the audit log, groups, roles, link types for all projects, the default theme, join requests, the Armature connection, and the owner and administrator roles.

No release has shipped, so removed addresses are deleted rather than redirected. Migrations take 00400 to 00419; M2's remaining ranges move to 00420 (#28), 00430 (#29) and 00440 (#30).

## Order

- [ ] #83 The browser suite isolates spec files without an organization each. This comes first.
- [ ] #84 One installation: the organization is made at first start, and a database with several stops.
- [ ] #85 Sign-in without organizations: no switching, one provider, no slug.
- [ ] #86 Members and administrators without organizations.
- [ ] #87 The Armature connection without an organization slug.
- [ ] #88 Say "everyone" instead of "the organization".
- [ ] #89 Docs, seed and deployment for one installation.
- [ ] #90 The integration suite isolates tests without an organization each.
- [ ] #91 Drop `org_id` and the tenant layer from the schema.

#87 depends only on #84 and can run beside #85 and #86.

## Out of scope

- Merging the data of several organizations.
- Running more than one team on one installation; that takes separate installations.

issues.title: Report the build at GET /api/v1/meta, as all three tools do
issues.body:
All three tools answer the same unauthenticated endpoint, so a partner, an operator or Dynamo can tell which build it talks to:

```
GET /api/v1/meta
{
  "product": "stator" | "armature" | "exciter",
  "build": { "version": "1.3.0", "commit": "abc1234", "builtAt": "2026-10-14T09:00:00Z" },
  "apiVersion": "1",
  "capabilities": []
}
```

- `version` is the semver from `VERSION` (a dev build says so, e.g. `1.3.0+4.gabc1234`), `commit` the short git hash, both stamped at build time.
- `apiVersion` is `info.version` of the OpenAPI document; it rises only for a change that breaks clients.
- `capabilities` is filled by the capability issue; until then it is an empty list.
- The endpoint is in the OpenAPI document and covered by a test that compares it with the build stamp.

**Here today:** `GET /api/v1/meta` returns `{product, build}` (also the MCP tool `server_info`). Add `apiVersion` and `capabilities`; the path stays.

issues.title: Release by tag the same way in all three tools
issues.body:
All three tools release the same way, following the release script of [chaosflix-jellyfin](https://github.com/praetorianer777/chaosflix-jellyfin/blob/main/release.sh) and its tag workflow:

- `./release.sh [version] [--dry-run]` infers the next semver from the Conventional Commits since the last tag (breaking: MAJOR, below 1.0.0 MINOR; `feat`: MINOR; `fix` and the rest: PATCH), or takes it by hand, and prints the rule it applied.
- It refuses a checkout that is behind its upstream or not on the default branch, so it never tags code the remote lacks.
- It writes the version into every file that carries one (`VERSION`, `web/package.json` where present, `Chart.yaml` `version` and `appVersion`), adds the CHANGELOG section and makes an annotated tag `vX.Y.Z` whose message is the release notes. A test refuses these files disagreeing.
- Main takes no direct commits here, so the bump travels on a branch `release/vX.Y.Z` with its own pull request; the tag is set on the merge commit (by the script after the merge, or by the workflow), never on a commit main does not have.
- On the tag, CI builds every image from the tag, pushes it to `ghcr.io/<owner>/<tool>-<image>:X.Y.Z` (and the commit hash), packages and publishes the chart, publishes the GitHub release from the tag message, and sends a `repository_dispatch` to Dynamo with the tool and version.
- A build not made from a tag says so in its version (`X.Y.Z+N.g<hash>`), so a dev image is never mistaken for a release.

**Here today:** `./release.sh` is Stator's copy, with the same gaps (no chart, no image push), and there is no chart yet.

issues.title: Give the webhook envelope a version
issues.body:
The webhook envelope carries a version, so its format can change without breaking receivers silently:

```
{ "version": 1, "id": "...", "topic": "issue.updated", "occurredAt": "...", "payload": { ... } }
```

- `version` is an integer and rises only for a change that breaks receivers (a field removed, renamed or changing meaning). Adding a field or a topic does not raise it.
- It is also sent as a header `X-<Product>-Webhook-Version`, so a receiver can decide before parsing.
- A sender of version N+1 keeps sending N to endpoints that registered for N, for at least one Dynamo release.
- A receiver ignores unknown fields and topics, and refuses an envelope version it does not know with a clear status and log line, instead of misreading it.
- The format is described in the OpenAPI document (or a JSON schema next to it) and covered by a contract test on both sides.

**Here:** Exciter will store issue status from Armature's webhooks and may send its own later. Build the receiver against the versioned envelope from the start, and use the same envelope for any webhook Exciter sends.

## What happened, and what did you expect?

`e2e/tests/themes.spec.ts` "a theme exported from Exciter imports again and draws the same, and so does one exported from Stator" fails now and then: `--color-primary` is still the previous theme's (`#b45309` where `#15803d` was expected, at line 139). issues.title: Speak the current MCP protocol
issues.body:
## User story

As someone connecting an assistant, I want Exciter's MCP endpoint to speak the protocol my client speaks and to describe its tools fully, so that the client connects without workarounds and the model knows what each tool answers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `initialize` offers `2025-11-25` and `2025-06-18`, answers the version the client asks for when it is one of them and the newest otherwise
- [ ] A request whose `MCP-Protocol-Version` header names a version Exciter does not speak is refused with 400 and a sentence naming the versions it does
- [ ] `GET /mcp` answers 405, since the endpoint opens no stream; an `Origin` that is not the installation's is refused on bearer calls as well as cookie ones
- [ ] `initialize` carries `instructions`: what a key such as `CHK-R42` is, that a text change needs `baseRevision`, how outlines number the document, and that reviews are decided by people in the browser
- [ ] Each tool has a `title`, an `outputSchema` drawn from its row's response type, and `structuredContent` that fits it
- [ ] Each tool is annotated `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint` and `idempotentHint` from its operation, and `openWorldHint` when it calls Armature or Stator
- [ ] `GET /meta` lists `mcp@1`, and `docs/integration.md` says what it promises
- [ ] `docs/mcp.md` says how to connect Claude Code and other MCP clients with a personal token

## Tests

Unit: version negotiation, the header refused, every tool's output schema built and every tool annotated. Integration: a conversation with the stack driven by the official Go SDK client (`github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`, in the test only): initialize, list the tools, call a read and a write, and read the API document resource; `GET /mcp` is 405; a foreign origin is refused.

## Implementation

- `backend/internal/httpapi/mcp.go` and `mcp_tools.go`; the output schemas come from `openapi.Builder` as the input schemas already do (`toolInput`).
- `instructions` is a constant beside `MCPProtocolVersion`, worded on Exciter's own terms.
- `mcp@1` joins the `capabilities` that `GET /meta` answers, with the others.

## Depends on

- #182

issues.body:
## User story

As someone connecting an assistant, I want to give it Exciter's address, sign in and say what it may do, so that a client that connects with an address alone can work with my requirements without me making and pasting a token.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (RFC 9728, also under the endpoint's path) names Exciter as the authorization server of `/api/v1/mcp`, and a 401 from `/mcp` carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="..."`
- [ ] `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414) describes the endpoints, `S256` and the grants offered
- [ ] A client is known by a Client ID Metadata Document, fetched through the outbound guard, or registers itself at `POST /oauth/register` (RFC 7591), limited in rate; a registration never used expires
- [ ] `GET /oauth/authorize` requires PKCE with `S256`, `state`, a redirect the client registered, and `resource` (RFC 8707) naming the MCP endpoint; each refusal is the error the RFC names, with a sentence
- [ ] The consent page `/oauth/consent` needs a session, names the client and the host it sends back to, and offers read-only or full and which projects, as a token does; allowing or denying returns to the client
- [ ] `POST /oauth/token` serves `authorization_code` and `refresh_token`; a code is used once; an access token lasts an hour and is stored only as its SHA-256; a refresh token turns over at each use, and one used twice ends the grant
- [ ] `POST /oauth/revoke` (RFC 7009) ends a token
- [ ] An OAuth access token is accepted at `/mcp` and for the calls it carries and nowhere else; read-only and the projects hold as for a personal token
- [ ] Switching somebody off ends their grants; administrators can switch OAuth connections off for the installation
- [ ] The audit log records `oauth.granted`

## Tests

Unit: PKCE verification, the metadata documents, the redirect match. Integration: the whole flow as a client makes it, then a tool call; a code used twice, a wrong verifier, an unregistered redirect and another resource each refused; a read-only grant refused a write; a grant limited to one project held by row level security, tried straight through SQL as `exciter_app`; a refresh token used twice ends the grant; an access token refused outside `/mcp`. Playwright: allow and deny on the consent page, with an accessibility check.

## Implementation

- A package `backend/internal/oauth` beside `internal/auth`, its tables in the contract's migration range with row level security that keeps a grant to its owner and administrators.
- `authenticate` (`backend/internal/httpapi/middleware.go`) knows the access token's prefix and puts a principal with the grant's limits on the request, as `authenticateAPIToken` does.
- The consent page reuses the scope and project choice of the token form (`web/src/features/tokens/TokensPage.tsx`).
- `netguard` fetches client metadata documents.

### What happened, and what did you expect?

`TestRawSQLKeepsWebhooksToAdministrators` fails now and then: the administrator reads 3 rows of their webhook and its log where the test expects 2, the endpoint and the ping. It failed once in M8 and twice in M9, and passed on every rerun.

Run `make test-integration` a few times; the race is timing dependent.

issues.body:
## User story

As somebody who moves or edits requirements in a project with computed attributes, I want my change to go through every time, even while the worker is still working values out.

## What happens

Moving a requirement sometimes answers 500. CI caught it on #247: `TestComputedAttributesFollowWhatTheyRead` failed with "move Pedal force into Brakes: got 500".

**Cause: a lock-order deadlock on `computed_dirty`.**
- A change's trigger upserts several marks, `ON CONFLICT (requirement_id) DO UPDATE`: the requirement, its old parent and its new parent.
- At the same time, the worker locks a batch of marks (`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), deletes them, and upserts marks for the parents and link neighbours of what it worked out.
- The deadlock: the change inserts the parent's mark, then waits on a mark the worker holds. The worker then waits on the parent's mark the change just inserted.
- Postgres kills one of the two. When it picks the change, the user sees a 500.

## Acceptance criteria

- A mark never waits on the worker: the queue is append-only, with no unique key and no foreign keys whose cascades or checks take locks.
- The worker takes a project's marks under its advisory lock. Several marks of one requirement count once, with the lowest step count.
- What happens is unchanged:
  - values are worked out again after a change;
  - roll-ups follow children and links;
  - the cycle stop still holds;
  - the recompute's progress counts requirements, not marks.
- Marks of deleted requirements or projects are dropped by the worker.

## Tests

- Integration: many concurrent moves and edits while the worker drains; every change succeeds, and the values settle as expected.
- The existing computed-attribute tests pass unchanged.

## Implementation

- Migration `01121_computed_queue.sql`:
  - re-creates `computed_dirty` with an identity key and no unique or foreign keys;
  - redefines `computed_mark`, `computed_recompute` and `computed_progress`.
- `attribute.Recomputer.batch` deletes the marks it takes with `RETURNING`, instead of locking them; `mark` inserts plainly.

issues.title: Give the database owner BYPASSRLS so a cnpg install can administer
issues.body:
## User story

As an operator installing Exciter with `cnpg.enabled`, I want the bootstrap and every administrator action to work, so that an installation on CloudNativePG is usable without a manual fix in the database.

Today the bootstrap Job stops at the identity provider:

```
seed failed: save the identity provider: ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy "oidc_provider_admins_only" for table "oidc_provider" (SQLSTATE 42501)
```

The permission functions are `SECURITY DEFINER` and read `app_user`, `org_member` and the other walled tables as the migration role that owns them. Those tables are `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, and their policies name `exciter_app` and `exciter_admin` only. In the compose stack and with the bundled Postgres the owner is a superuser, which passes every policy, so nothing noticed. Under cnpg the chart makes the owner `exciter_owner`, neither superuser nor `BYPASSRLS`: `current_actor_administers()` sees no account and answers false for everybody, so the bootstrap administrator may not save a provider, and no administrator may do anything walled.

## Acceptance criteria

- With `cnpg.enabled`, the Cluster lists the owner role under `managed.roles` with `bypassrls: true`, so the operator grants it on a fresh install and on an existing one at the next reconcile.
- `migrate up`, `up-to` and `down` refuse an owner that is neither superuser nor `BYPASSRLS`, with a sentence saying what to grant, so an external database with such an owner fails at the migration instead of at the first administrator action.
- `docs/deployment.md` says what the owner needs; `docs/decisions.md` records why.

## Tests

- `tests/test-helm.sh`: the cnpg render gives the owner `bypassrls: true`, with its own password Secret; the golden `tests/helm/production.yaml` is regenerated.
- Integration: a role made `NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS` is refused by the owner check, and passes once it is altered to `BYPASSRLS`.

## Implementation

- `deploy/charts/exciter/templates/cnpg-cluster.yaml`: add the owner to the managed roles, with the `dbOwner` Secret.
- `backend/migrations`: an owner check the migrate command runs before it changes the schema.

issues.title: Keep the outbox tests from racing the stack's worker
issues.body:
`TestTheWorkerHoldsNoLockWhileItHandles` (backend/test/outbox_test.go) fails by chance, so any PR's CI can go red without a cause in the PR. It failed on #277, whose change does not touch the outbox, and passed when CI ran again:

```
outbox_test.go:312: the stack's worker took every one of 5 events first
--- FAIL: TestTheWorkerHoldsNoLockWhileItHandles (25.10s)
```

**Why it fails:** the test plants an event in the shared `outbox_event` table and waits for its own worker to claim it, but the stack's worker polls the same table. Whichever claims first wins. The test gives up after `claimTries` (5) offers of `claimWait` (5 s) each, so on a busy runner, or when the stack's worker polls more often than the test's, the stack's worker can take all five. The other tests that use `claimTries` (the `offerer`) depend on the same race.

**What would make it reliable:** the test's worker has to be the only one able to claim its events. For example:
- plant the test's events under a topic or partition that the stack's worker does not claim, or
- pause the stack's worker for the test, or
- give the claim query a filter that only the test's worker passes.

Retrying more times only makes the failure rarer.

**Done when:** the outbox tests never depend on beating the stack's worker, and the integration layer passes them on a loaded runner, for example with `go test -count=20 -run 'Outbox|Worker'` against the running stack.

issues.title: Architecture drawings in PlantUML, drawn in every view and edited as text
issues.body:
## User story

As a systems engineer, I want to draw architecture diagrams in PlantUML inside a requirement, so that the structure a requirement asks for is shown beside its words and stays editable as text that is versioned with it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The editor inserts a PlantUML diagram into a statement, rationale or rich text value; it is edited as PlantUML text with a live preview below it
- [ ] Every view that shows a requirement's text shows the drawn picture: the requirement, the document view, history, baselines, comparisons and print
- [ ] A diagram that cannot be drawn shows its source and the first line of why; a server without a renderer shows the source and says so
- [ ] Only the PlantUML text is stored; history diffs it as text and search finds its words
- [ ] Markdown in and out writes a diagram as a `plantuml` fenced block; ReqIF, CSV and Excel carry the source
- [ ] PDF, Word and the static site show the picture; Word embeds it as PNG and falls back to the source with a note
- [ ] Diagrams are drawn by a Kroki container that only the api reaches, in its secure mode, so a diagram can include no file or address; compose and the Helm chart ship it pinned

## Tests

Go unit: the allowlist's diagram node and its limits, the Markdown fence both ways, the source diff, the Kroki client (SVG, PNG, syntax error, timeout, busy, cache, size cap), Word with a picture and with the fallback, the settings. Integration against the stack's Kroki: the route draws, refuses broken source with Kroki's sentence and refuses an include, search finds a diagram's words, Markdown keeps it, Word holds the PNG. vitest: the figure, its fallbacks and the editor node. Playwright: add a diagram, type PlantUML, watch the preview, save, see the picture on the requirement and in the document view, with an accessibility check.

## Implementation

- A `diagram` block node (`language`: `plantuml`, `source`: up to 20000 characters), adapted from Stator's diagram node.
- `internal/diagram`: a Kroki client modelled on `internal/render`, with a small cache, behind `POST /api/v1/diagrams`; `EXCITER_KROKI_URL`, `_TIMEOUT`, `_CONCURRENCY`, blank leaving drawing off.
- The web shows the SVG as a `data:` image, so nothing in it runs and the CSP stays as it is.
- Migration range 01380 to 01399: search reads a diagram's source.

## Depends on

Nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

issues.title: Stop test-release.sh failing on a leftover git process
issues.body:
`tests/test-release.sh` fails by chance in the "shell and format" job. It failed on `main` at d6dd00c8:

```
The test fixture broke while removing the previous case's repository. The error above is the cause; fix it and run the script again.
```

**Cause:** `use_fixture` removes the previous case's `repo` and `repo.remote` before copying the next one. A git process the previous case left behind can still be writing into the remote, so `rm -rf` fails on a directory that isn't empty. Stator had the same fixture and the same failure (praetorianer777/Stator#475, fixed in praetorianer777/Stator#476).

**Fix:** give each case a directory of its own (`repo-1`, `repo-2`, ...) instead of removing the last one. The `EXIT` trap still removes everything.

## Done when
- `use_fixture` no longer removes anything.
- `tests/test-release.sh` passes.

issues.title: Let release.sh cut a release with a long commit history
issues.body:
`release.sh` passes the commits since the last tag to Python in the environment variable `RAW_LOG`. Before the first tag that's the whole history, now 120 KB on `main`, and Linux refuses any single environment string over 128 KB (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`). A few more commits and `./release.sh` fails before writing anything with "python3: Argument list too long". Stator hit exactly this (praetorianer777/Stator#485, fixed in praetorianer777/Stator#486). The release commit's `-m "$(cat notes)"` has the same limit.

**Fix:** as in Stator: the log goes to a temporary file whose path Python reads, and the commit uses `-F`.

## Done when
- `tests/test-release.sh` has a first release with a history far over 128 KB, and it passes.

issues.title: Shard the integration tests in CI
issues.body:
In CI, `test-integration` is the slowest job: about 10 minutes in a single job on the last green `main`. The whole run takes about as long as that job. Stator runs the same layer as 3 jobs of about 6 minutes each, each with its own stack.

**Change:** split `test-integration` into shards, as Stator does:
- `mk/go.mk` lists the tests with `go test -list`, and a `SHARD=i/n` variable picks every n-th one into `-run`;
- CI runs a matrix of 3 jobs, each starting its own stack, and the report job merges their JSON reports.

Pick the shard count from the measured time, so no shard runs much over 4 minutes.

## Done when
- CI's integration jobs each take at most about 4 to 5 minutes, and the report still lists every test once.
- `make test-integration` without `SHARD` still runs everything locally.

issues.title: Find why /risks answered 500 in the FMEA timing test
issues.body:
On `main` at 50087fed, `TestTheFMEATableReadsManyRisksInGoodTime` (`backend/test/risk_mitigations_test.go:255`) failed:

```
/risks?limit=200: got 500, want 200: {"error":{"code":"internal_error",...,"requestId":"40a4193d-a23b-4531-b756-5a1d0afc7534"}}
```

It passed on fe745e6f, and the only change between them was `release.sh`. It also passed 10 of 10 times locally on its own. So it fails only some of the time, probably under the load of the whole suite.

**What's missing:** the cause. The test talks to the stack's api container, which logs `request failed` with the error. CI keeps the test reports but not the stack's logs, so request 40a4193d can't be traced.

**Leads:**
- `risk.Service.Rows` reads through `db.Read`, which routes to the streaming replica (`hot_standby=on`). A long read there can be cancelled with "canceling statement due to conflict with recovery" (SQLSTATE 40001) while the primary vacuums, which comes back as a 500. `hot_standby_feedback` isn't set.
- Alternatively, a statement or request timeout under CI's load: the test writes 100 risks with 300 links just before.

**Fix:**
1. CI keeps `docker compose logs` of the stack as an artifact when a stack layer fails.
2. With the cause known: fix it at its source. For a replica conflict, that means `hot_standby_feedback=on` on the replica, or retrying a read cancelled for recovery on the primary. Don't loosen the test.

## Done when
- A failed CI run keeps the stack's logs.
- The cause is named here, and the fix makes the test pass 20 times in a row inside a full suite run.

issues.title: Sign in silently when the identity provider already has a session
issues.body:
Someone signed in to Armature, Stator or Exciter through the suite's Keycloak realm, who then opens another of the three, lands on its sign-in page and has to click "Sign in". Keycloak still has their session, so the click sends them there and straight back, signed in, without a password. The click is all that's left, but it happens on every first visit and on every link from one tool to another. This was seen on a real Dynamo install, where Keycloak returns at once.

**Change:** on a visit without a session, Exciter first tries a silent sign-in:
- **The request:** a top-level redirect to the provider's authorization endpoint with `prompt=none`, the usual `state`, PKCE and `nonce`, and the page the person asked for.
- **Keycloak still has a session:** the callback signs the person in, as a normal sign-in does, with the same group mapping and membership checks, and returns them to that page.
- **No session** (`error=login_required`, `interaction_required` or `consent_required`): the callback shows the sign-in page as today, and remembers for the browser session (a short-lived cookie) that the silent try already failed, so there's no redirect loop and no second round trip on the next page.
- **Only when single sign-on is configured:** with local accounts only, nothing changes.
- **Not after signing out:** a sign-out sets the same marker, so the person isn't signed straight back in. With RP-initiated logout at the provider, the provider's session ends too.
- **Can be turned off:** a setting, for example `auth.silentSignIn` in the chart, on by default when an OIDC provider is set.

## Done when
- In the integration or browser tests, with a provider that has a session, opening a deep link without a session lands on that page signed in, with no click. Without a provider session, it lands on the sign-in page, and the next page doesn't redirect again.
- After signing out, the next visit shows the sign-in page.
- `GET /api/v1/meta` lists `auth.silent-sign-in@1`, so the suite's tests can rely on it (praetorianer777/Dynamo#2).

issues.title: Send relation requirement with the remote links synced to Armature
issues.body:
When Exciter syncs a trace link to Armature, it puts the requirement on the issue through `POST /issues/{issueKey}/remote-links` with `url`, `title`, `source` and `iconUrl`, but no `relation` (`backend/internal/armature/sync.go`, `RemoteLinkRequest`). Armature then files it as a `page`, so the issue shows the requirement it implements among its pages.

Armature's remote links take `relation: requirement` for "a requirement the issue implements" (`backend/internal/issue/remotelinks.go`, `RemoteLinkRequirement`); sending a url already there updates the relation when one is sent, so existing links would be corrected on the next sync.

Seen in Dynamo's sample import (praetorianer777/Dynamo#24) against Exciter 0.1.0 and Armature 0.1.0: `GET /api/v1/issues/SPARK-1/remote-links` lists the Exciter requirement with `"relation":"page"`, though Exciter traced SPARK-R1 to SPARK-1 as `implements`.

**Expected:** the remote link of an `implements` (and `verifies`) trace carries `relation: requirement`, when Armature's capabilities list it.

issues.title: Make a provider group before its first member signs in
issues.body:
Exciter learns a sign-in provider's group only when one of its members signs in (groups are synced at sign-in, `GET /groups` only). So an administrator, or Dynamo's connect job, cannot grant a realm group access to a project (`PUT /projects/{key}/grants`) before anyone in that group has signed in.

Armature already allows it: `POST /groups` with `name` and `externalRef`, matched to the claim at sign-in.

## Done when
- `POST /groups` with `name` and `externalRef` makes a provider group that a later sign-in with that group in its claim joins, instead of making a second one.
- A second request for the same `externalRef` answers 409, or returns the group, as Armature does.
- The group can be named in project permissions straight away.
- Integration test: make the group, grant it on a project, sign in a person of that group, and they see the project.

Needed so the three tools can grant the same access per group (praetorianer777/Dynamo, issue filed with this one).

issues.title: Map a provider group to a read-only standing
issues.body:
A group mapping (`POST /oidc-provider/group-roles`) grants only `member` or `admin` (`grouproles.go`). A realm group of readers therefore gets every grant `everyone` has, such as editing each new project, with no way to admit them read-only by group.

- Integration test: a person in a group mapped this way can sign in and read a project open to everyone, and cannot change it.

Asked for so the three tools give a realm group of readers the same standing everywhere (see the Dynamo issue filed with this one).
